overview: A translated telegram received from Bern on January 4, 1944, reports a Japanese government reorganization effective November 1, 1943. Japan combined its Ministries of Communications and Railroads to create the Ministry of Transport and Communications and established an Administration Council of Posts and Telegraphs to oversee postal, telegraph, money-order, and savings-account services. The telegram also identifies the senior officials appointed to the reorganized agencies.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Bern on Japanese transport and communications reorganization
subfiles.about: Reports the creation of Japan’s Ministry of Transport and Communications and the appointment of officials to the reorganized postal and telegraph administration.
subfiles.summary: This translated telegram conveys a Japanese government notice that, effective November 1, 1943, the Ministries of Communications and Railroads had been combined into a new Ministry of Transport and Communications. An Administration Council of Posts and Telegraphs was established to administer posts, telegraphs, postal money orders, and savings accounts. Yoshiaki Hatta was named minister, Shigeru Komatsu president of the new council, and Junichi Nakamura director general of posts and telegraphs.

interest: The telegram provides a concise contemporary record of Japan’s wartime consolidation of transportation and communications administration. It is particularly useful for establishing the reorganization’s effective date, institutional structure, assigned responsibilities, and senior personnel. The document also illustrates how information about Japanese domestic administration reached the U.S. State Department through neutral Bern during World War II.
